title: Tool adapter profile
description: profile.yaml, the declarative part of a tool adapter: how the tool is detected, where its configuration lives and where each kind of artifact goes. Wherever a directory or file is named, the value is a path template: "{name}" stands for the root of that name, and a path starting with "~/" lies in the home directory. Forward slashes on every platform.

id.description: The stable identifier of the tool, such as "claude-code". Recorded in the manifest; it cannot change after a release.

name.description: The tool's own name, such as "Claude Code". A proper name, not translated.

detect.description: How to tell whether the tool is installed: one of the executables is on the PATH, or one of the directories exists.

dirs.description: Directories that only exist when the tool has been used.

version.description: How to ask the tool for its version.

run.description: The command and its arguments, such as [opencode, --version].

match.description: A regular expression (RE2 syntax) whose first group is the version.

roots.description: The directories everything else is relative to, by name. A root is the environment variable's value with "join" appended when the variable holds an absolute path, and "default" otherwise.

env.description: The environment variable that moves this root.

join.description: Appended to the variable's value, for variables that name a parent directory.

default.description: Where the root is when the variable is not set.

verified.description: How the facts in this profile were checked against the real tool, in enough detail for anyone to repeat it. A profile without this record is inert: nothing is ever written to a tool nobody has checked.

version.description: The version of the tool that was checked. Quote it, so that 2.10 does not become the number 2.1.

os.description: The operating systems it was checked on.

at.description: The date of the check, as YYYY-MM-DD.

how.description: What was done, such as running the tool's own command in a temporary home directory and reading the file it wrote.

layout.description: What an entry is. "dir": every skill is a directory of its own.

commands.description: Where the tool keeps slash commands, one file each.

agents.description: Where the tool keeps sub-agents, one file each.

mcp.description: Where the tool keeps its MCP servers.

files.description: The configuration file, for tools that accept more than one name. The one that exists is used; when none exists the last one is created.

format.description: The syntax of the file. "json" is strict JSON; "jsonc" allows comments and trailing commas, and both are preserved.

path.description: The key under which the servers are listed, one element per level. Each server becomes one more key below it.

alsoReads.description: Directories of other tools that this tool reads as well. A resource another tool's plan already puts there is not written a second time for this tool.

kind.description: What the tool reads from the directory.

credentials.description: Names of files that hold the tool's credentials. A preview never copies a file with one of these names into its temporary directory.

pathTemplate.description: A path that starts with "~/" or with a root in braces, such as "~/.claude/skills" or "{config}/skills". Forward slashes only.

ext.description: The file extension, with its dot.
